name: Cartesia Sonic 3.5
access: Cartesia TTS API: Bytes (HTTP), SSE and WebSocket, model_id sonic-3.5 or the dated snapshot sonic-3.5-2026-05-04
Cartesia Playground and Managed Agents (Ink and Sonic)

voice.input_audio: none: the model takes text, with optional SSML-like tags (emotion, speed, volume, break, spell) and [laughter]
voice.output_audio: Containers: raw (all endpoints), wav and mp3 (the Bytes endpoint only). Encodings: pcm_f32le, pcm_s16le, pcm_mulaw, pcm_alaw. Sample rates: 8000, 16000, 22050, 24000, 44100 and 48000 Hz [cart-format]
voice.voices: 500+ built-in voices; custom cloning: instant voice clones from a short clip and professional voice clones from 30+ minutes of audio per the cloning guide (the Sonic product page says 15 to 30 minutes) [cart-voices] [cart-ivc] [cart-site]
voice.latency: Cartesia's model page for 3.5 states sub-90 ms latency without a measurement path [cart-sonic35]
voice.session_limit: A WebSocket context expires 1 second after the last audio is streamed out [cart-contexts]; the longest transcript per request was not found in the pages read

pricing_usd_per_mtok.notes: Per character, not per token. Cartesia bills credits, and one credit is one character; about 750 to 800 credits make a minute of audio. Plans: Free US$0 (20K credits), Pro US$5 (100K), Startup US$49 (1.25M), Scale US$299 (8M) and Enterprise (custom). Overage is US$65 per 1M credits on Pro, US$45 on Startup and US$38 on Scale [cart-pricing]. Contexts add no separate charge [cart-contexts]. Artificial Analysis lists US$49 per 1M characters [aa-tts-board]
